label: Speech recognition & diarization
note: Recognition is used three different ways here — as a transcript, as the timing source for narration, and as a judge of whether a sung line is intelligible. The same model behaves differently in each role.

entities.name: Whisper base/tiny (openai-whisper)
entities.summary: The original transcription path. tiny deliberately survives in one place: murch_engine transcribes known TTS narration only for word TIMINGS and then force-aligns to the real script, so a better model buys nothing there.

issues.text: Word recognition was not good enough for clip analysis and subtitles.
Kept on tiny in murch_engine on purpose — the words are discarded, only the timings are used.

entities.name: faster-whisper large-v3 + VAD
entities.summary: One shared VRAM-aware loader with VAD filtering and a model cache. It is also the recogniser the kids-music lyric gate decodes with, which is where its prompting behaviour became a correctness problem.

issues.text: Replaced base/tiny for real transcripts, with a CPU-degrade rule that drops to base+beam1 rather than large-v3 — large-v3 on CPU stalls for HOURS on long media.

PROMPTED decoding invents what it was told to expect: prompting with the lyric sheet was worth ~+22 points of coverage and passed 33 lines a listener cannot make out, including a hook heard 0/5 times unprompted. The gate now decodes BARE on the mix as well and judges clarity on that number.

Validating a prompted recogniser against SILENCE proves nothing — digital silence gives the prompt nothing to hang on, while a line sung as mush still has audio. The old muted-line test was true and irrelevant.
Unprompted scores carry about ±1 line of run-to-run jitter, so single-line differences are noise.
The resident model stays large-v2, not v3-turbo, pending a real-audio A/B.

entities.name: whisper large-v3-turbo
entities.summary: Measured and held, not adopted: it tied on accuracy and only won on speed, which was not enough to move the resident model.

issues.text: Tied WER with faster-whisper large-v2 on the synthetic set at 18% faster — held pending a real-audio A/B that was never run.

entities.name: NeMo Sortformer 4-spk
entities.summary: There was ZERO diarization before this. Runs as a subprocess in its own venv so its torch cannot collide with the pipeline's, and the bridge is fail-safe: any failure returns None and the transcript is still emitted.

issues.text: Added speaker separation where there was none, pinned by ZYG_SORTFORMER_MODEL.
Offline with a ~12-minute VRAM ceiling, so long audio must be chunked (600 s windows) and the speakers re-identified globally.
Temporal-overlap stitching across chunks fragmented one speaker into two and could exceed the 4-speaker cap — replaced by TitaNet embedding clustering with a hard cap.

entities.name: TitaNet-large
entities.summary: Agglomerative cosine clustering over TitaNet embeddings gives a speaker a stable identity across chunks. It is also the similarity metric that built the Warm Control voice-conversion dataset.

issues.text: Fixed the cross-chunk fragmentation that overlap stitching caused, hard-capped at 4 speakers.
Re-used outside diarization to select RVC training renditions by cosine to the reference take — the v2 dataset that passed the bench.

entities.name: pyannote
entities.role: diarization in the standalone transcriber app
entities.where: a separate transcriber app, outside this repository
entities.summary: The standalone transcriber app keeps pyannote rather than Sortformer — deliberately not unified, because the 07-28 rebuild turned out to have targeted the video pipeline and not that app.

issues.text: Two diarization stacks exist in the program for historical reasons; neither has been measured against the other.
